diagnostics.message: The engine did not claim normality from a small-sample significance test; inspect the replicate distribution and study design.
Student's t-test uses a pooled variance and therefore assumes equal population variances; selecting it records acceptance of that stronger assumption.
Mann-Whitney U evaluates rank/distributional ordering under the selected alternative; it is not automatically a test of medians without additional distributional assumptions.
The paired t-test concerns the distribution of within-unit differences, not either condition separately.
Wilcoxon signed-rank evaluates the distribution of non-zero within-unit differences and requires valid stable-unit pairing.
Welch ANOVA and Games-Howell comparisons do not assume equal group variances; biological-unit independence remains a design requirement.
Conventional one-way ANOVA and its pooled-variance comparisons assume equal population variances.
Conventional one-way ANOVA and its pooled-variance comparisons assume equal population variances.

Only the explicitly selected pairwise comparisons were tested with Holm-adjusted p-values. Simultaneous confidence intervals are not reported for this workflow.
Kruskal-Wallis is reported as an omnibus rank test only; no unvalidated pairwise post-hoc tests were generated.
D04 used complete matched units only; row order was not used to infer correspondence.
The initial repeated-measures ANOVA does not estimate a sphericity correction; use a mixed model when this assumption is not defensible.
Pairwise confidence intervals use a Bonferroni simultaneous level while pairwise p-values use Holm adjustment.
D05 used sum-to-zero contrasts and Type III tests; inspect the interaction before interpreting averaged main effects.
All-cell confidence intervals use a Bonferroni simultaneous level while pairwise p-values use Holm adjustment.
Correlation describes association and does not establish causation.
